findings.title: Preserve row-level unavailable identity errors during cleanup retries
findings.body: `unavailable` is treated as a failed identity observation when deciding to enter the retry block, but the loop stops as soon as `checkWindowsProcesses` resolves, even when the returned rows still have `status: 'unavailable'`. Such failures therefore receive only one read-only retry instead of up to three. Additionally, if the initial call returned an unavailable row with its `error`, the successful retry overwrites `processes`; that original error is never added to `errors`, so transient diagnostic evidence is lost. Accumulate unavailable-row errors before replacing the result and continue read-only retries for unavailable rows until every identity has a terminal status or three attempts are exhausted. Persistent unavailable results must continue to leave `mainExited` false.

overall_explanation: The lifecycle-tree retry is correct: it performs at most three read-only samples, records every unknown/source-unknown sample, and lets the original assertions fail on persistent unknown. The Electron cleanup retry is incomplete because row-level `unavailable` results stop the loop and can have their error evidence overwritten by a later successful observation. This violates the stated three-attempt, retained-error behavior.
